context.note: The work order's references were narrowed against the authorized paths when it was authorized, and the profile's ceiling bounds how many further capsules the assembler may add. `refs` is what the packet actually carries - there is no wider set behind it and no scoped list beside it.

advisory_only: max_turns: no backend this company drives accepts a turn ceiling
company_enforces: developer_attempts: the job state machine refuses a further attempt
context_refs: the packet is built from the narrowed set
enforcement.note: Company OS does not start a process and therefore enforces nothing inside a session. What it can do is refuse to issue the next one.
runner_enforces: wall_seconds: the runner terminates the session process
session_cost: passed to the backend when the backend accepts one

resource_ceiling.escalation_message: Stop and report progress rather than exceeding these ceilings. An honest partial result with a checkpoint is cheaper than a complete one that ran out of budget.

efficiency.strategy_reason: reasoning class C at risk low is routine implementation; profile consumer runs it at the standard tier; evidence is required and affects review depth, not model tier; review session: read-only with reduced context budget

work_order.objective: The CEO result page (EngineeringResult) reports how many developer attempts a job has used (developer_attempts) but never how many remain against the work order's own authorized ceiling, so reading the page requires separately looking up max_developer_attempts and subtracting by hand every time. Add a field to EngineeringResult reporting the developer attempts remaining, populated from the job's own existing corrections_remaining property (do not reimplement the arithmetic), and show it on the CEO page's text rendering next to the existing developer attempts line.
